provenance.method: Bounded review of current Microsoft Windows accessibility support documentation; feature availability remains version-dependent.

name: Microsoft Windows accessibility features
description: Microsoft support hub for Windows accessibility features spanning vision, hearing, mobility, input and focus, including voice typing and voice access.
intended_use: Inspecting built-in Windows settings before buying or installing another accessibility tool.
audience_or_context: Windows users; exact features depend on Windows version, language, hardware and region.
limitations: Vendor documentation describes product features, not independent evidence that a feature will suit a particular person.
Feature names and availability can change with operating-system updates.
cost_or_access_notes: Many listed features are built into supported Windows versions; device and software costs are separate.
conflicts_of_interest: Microsoft develops and sells Windows; ND Oracle lists first-party feature documentation rather than treating it as independent efficacy evidence.
